input.answer: I'd go with the third one. It's the same table, but the left column only says "מט"ח עד 10%" or "120%", with no "מניות עד 120%" line that made me go "how do you have 120% in stocks?". The name, what it follows and the fee read the same on all three. I'm not very sure, the three look almost the same.

stuck.where: Fee column, three lines per fund (קבוע / משתנים / נאמן)
stuck.why: I wanted one fee number per fund. With three I couldn't tell which one I actually pay, so I just looked at the top one, קבוע, 0.8% for S&P against 0.1% for TA-90.
120% of something sounded wrong or risky. I didn't get it and stopped on it.
They look almost identical. I had to look back and forth to find what moved: the left column, and a profile line under the index in option 2.

used: Fund names on the right (S&P 500, MSCI AC World, ת"א-125, ת"א-90)
Top fee line "קבוע" in each row

Tags "עסקת החלף" and "מס גם על שינויי המטבע"

Fee in shekels (what it would cost me on 30,000 ₪)

findings.what: The fee is split into three percentages with no total, so I can't tell what a fund costs me. I only read the first one.
"מניות עד 120%" looks like a mistake or something scary, and nothing next to it explains it.
findings.where: Left column in option 1, profile line in option 2

findings.what: "מס גם על שינויי המטבע" reads like a warning on the S&P and World funds, and those are the ones I came for.
findings.where: Tags under the S&P 500 / MSCI rows

findings.what: The fee and exposure columns sit at the far left, so I reach them last and easily miss them.
The three options are nearly the same, so it's hard to see what changed.
No fee in shekels. 0.8% doesn't feel like much money to me.
